recipe_version.title: Persian Ash Reshteh: Herb, Bean, and Noodle Soup with Kashk and Mint Oil
recipe_version.description: A thick soup of green lentils, chickpeas, and kidney beans simmered in vegetable broth with turmeric and heaps of parsley, cilantro, dill, spinach, and scallions, thickened with broken linguine, and topped with tangy kashk, deep-brown onions, garlic, and dried mint bloomed in oil.

ingredients.name: vegetable broth

ingredients.name: chickpeas
ingredients.display_name: chickpeas (one 15-oz can) whose label lists chickpeas, water, and salt

ingredients.name: red kidney beans
ingredients.display_name: red kidney beans (one 15-oz can) whose label lists beans, water, and salt

ingredients.display_name: liquid kashk whose label lists whey, water, and salt
ingredients.note: thinned with a spoonful of the soup if very thick

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Rinse the lentils, drain and rinse the chickpeas and kidney beans, wash and chop the parsley, cilantro, dill, and spinach, slice the scallions, and thinly slice the onions and garlic.

steps.title: Start the soup
steps.body: Put the lentils, broth, 2 cups water, turmeric, and salt in the 6-quart Dutch oven. Bring to a boil over high, about 10 minutes to come to a boil, then simmer until the lentils are nearly tender, about 20 minutes.

steps.title: Herbs and noodles
steps.body: Add the chickpeas, kidney beans, parsley, cilantro, dill, spinach, scallions, and pepper and simmer 10 minutes. Add the linguine and simmer, stirring from the bottom often, until tender and the soup is thick, about 12 minutes.

steps.title: Onions, garlic, and mint
steps.body: While the soup simmers (overlap stated): heat the oil in the 10-inch skillet over medium and cook the onions, stirring often, until deep brown, about 15 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute, then lift the onions and garlic onto a plate. Take the skillet off the heat and stir the dried mint into the oil for 10 seconds.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Stir half the onions and 1/4 cup kashk into the soup. Ladle into bowls and top each with a drizzle of kashk, the remaining onions and garlic, and a spoon of mint oil.

coverage_contribution: Persia has ghormeh sabzi, koobideh, and sabzi polo in the catalog, all with meat or fish; there is no Persian vegetarian soup and no legume-herb-noodle soup. A vegetarian dinner with real heft.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with persian-ghormeh-sabzi: a vegetarian soup of legumes, herbs, and noodles with kashk, not a lamb and dried-lime herb stew over rice. Compared with white-bean-kale-soup: three legumes, five herbs and greens, and noodles with tangy kashk, not a simple bean-and-kale broth. Compared with egyptian-koshari: a herb soup with noodles in it, not lentils, rice, and pasta under tomato sauce.
not_duplicate_of: Not minestrone (no tomato, Persian herbs and kashk) and not a lentil soup.
